title: When you land
body:
Izumo Enmusubi Airport (IZO) is the practical gateway to Shimane — no international flights, so you connect through Tokyo (HND/NRT), Osaka (KIX/ITM), or another domestic hub. The terminal is small: one baggage carousel, a taxi rank, and a connecting bus stop just outside arrivals.

An airport limousine bus meets each arriving flight (departs roughly 10 minutes after baggage claim opens) and runs two routes — one toward Matsue, one toward Izumo city. Confirm which one you need before boarding; they don't both stop at Izumo Taisha.

⚠ Bus frequency and the exact Matsue-route stop list should be reconfirmed close to your dates — it's a small regional service and schedules move around seasonally.

title: Local essentials
body:
Shimane is cash-first outside the two main stations. ICOCA/Suica-type IC cards work on JR around Matsue — the JR West ICOCA area on the San-in Line reaches west only as far as Izumo-shi Station, and one stop beyond it, toward Oda and Omori, you're back to paper tickets and coins. Off JR, don't assume either: neither the Ichibata Electric Railway nor the Iwami Kotsu buses out to Omori publish IC acceptance on their own pages, so treat every non-JR leg of this trip as a cash leg until a gate proves otherwise.

Convenience stores (7-Eleven, Lawson) have ATMs that reliably accept foreign cards; rural Oda/Omori has far fewer of them than Matsue, so withdraw before the transfer day, not after.

title: Entry & documents
body: US passport holders are ordinarily visa-exempt for short tourist stays in Japan (commonly cited as up to 90 days), with a Visit Japan Web pre-registration for the immigration/customs QR codes. ⚠ The current rule could not be confirmed directly against Japan's own immigration ministry page — both mofa.go.jp and the nearest US–Japan consulate page refused a direct, non-browser fetch (HTTP 403). Re-verify against MOFA's official visa-exemption page or a Japanese consulate before booking, and check each traveler's own passport country if the party isn't all US citizens.

title: Phone & data
body: ⚠ Cellular coverage specifically inside the Omori valley / Ryugenji Mabu trail hasn't been confirmed — rural mountain valleys in Japan can have dead spots, but no source-backed claim either way exists yet. Download offline maps for the Omori townscape and the mine-trail route before you leave Matsue as a precaution, not because a gap is confirmed.

title: Booking checklist
body:
Two things need booking earlier than the rest: Omori lodging (the heritage machiya inns are genuinely small — see Days) and any soba-house meal for the full party of 8 (none of the shortlisted places publish a group-capacity figure, so a phone call to confirm seating beats a walk-in).

If the village stay (Takyo-Abeke) is chosen over the Oda City hotel alternative: the operator opens bookings on the 1st of each month for stays 6 months out, so this trip's window opened 2026-04-01 — book now, since it needs two separate reservations (main house + storehouse) and both staying available this close in isn't guaranteed. No deposit is required, but cancelling the day before or day of arrival costs a 100% fee.
checklist: Flights into Izumo (IZO) or a connecting hub
Matsue lodging, 2 nights — accessible/step-free room for the 2 low-mobility travelers

Oda/Omori lodging, 1 night — book as one party-of-8 block early; heritage inns split across buildings past 6 guests (Takyo-Abeke's 2026-04-01 booking window is already open; free cancellation only 2+ days out)
Phone call ahead to any soba/kaiseki restaurant for a party of 8

title: Weather for your dates
note: Late Oct in Matsue averages a 22°C high / 13°C low with ≈126mm of rain across the month (1991–2020 normal) — still inside Japan's typhoon season tail, so a wet-weather day is a real possibility, not just a forecast quirk.
